BiblicalUsage: The word is the royal edict, the law of the Medes and Persians that cannot be changed. Daniel's enemies use the king's own law against him, and the decree stands even when the king regrets it. Ezra carries the law of the king of kings alongside it, and the two laws meet in the exile's life.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the edict shows the limit of human law: a king can sign what he cannot undo, but the law of God stands above every decree of men. The king's law can bind a man, but it cannot bind the God who overrules it.
